terms.definition: A chemical bond formed when electrons are transferred and the resulting oppositely charged ions attract.
terms.function: Builds ionic compounds like salts by locking positive and negative ions together.
terms.whereItIs: The attraction between Na⁺ and Cl⁻ in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Ionic bonds build table salt and the minerals of the Earth.

terms.definition: The complete movement of an electron from one atom to another.
terms.function: Turns the giver positive and the taker negative, setting up the attraction.
terms.whereItIs: The traveling dot along the path between the two atoms.
terms.whyItMatters: Transferring, not sharing, is what makes the bond ionic.

terms.definition: An atom that has lost or gained electrons and therefore carries a charge.
terms.function: The charged particles that an ionic bond locks together.
terms.whereItIs: Na⁺ and Cl⁻ — the two atoms after the transfer.
terms.whyItMatters: Ions are the building blocks of ionic compounds.

terms.definition: A repeating 3D grid of alternating positive and negative ions.
terms.function: The structure that holds an ionic compound like salt together as a solid.
terms.whereItIs: The cube of alternating violet and green cells in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: The lattice structure is why salt forms crystals and melts at high temperature.
